root_idea.summary: The root centers on settling or remaining attached to something, yielding the ideas of continuity, persistence, and lasting duration.
root_idea.development: From stillness and abiding, the lexicon develops meanings of enduring over time, making something lasting, continuous rain, and related derived senses such as apparent suspension or circling. Some derived usages extend metaphorically to moderation, waiting, and seeking continuance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form دَامَ.
Displayed under the normalized singular active-participle citation form دَائِمٌ.

senses.definition: To continue, remain, or endure over a period of time.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it occurs in ما دام temporal constructions, meaning “as long as,” “while,” or “for as long as” someone or something remains in a stated condition.

senses.definition: Continuing, enduring, lasting, or constant; perpetual or everlasting.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally or predicatively for something enduring, as with everlasting fruit, and for persons constant in a sustained practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persist in or adhere continually to an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى or عَلَيْهِ for continued adherence to a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become still or motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to water left in a pool, to the sea, or to the boiling of a cooking-pot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become tired or fatigued.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived, figurative use associated with stopping to rest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go round, revolve, or circle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to circling movement, including a bird circling around water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a bucket to become full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is explained with reference to the water becoming settled in the bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the sky to rain continuously or consecutively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sustained rainfall; the attested expression is دَوَّمَتِ السَّمَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go far or continue one’s course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of dogs or horses in pursuit or running; some authorities explain the cited poetic usage differently.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To circle or hover in the air.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a bird circling or rising high in the sky, sometimes appearing nearly stationary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spinning top or other round object made to revolve by a string.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is associated with the act of making the object revolve so rapidly that it appears still.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the sun to circle in the sky and appear stationary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the sun’s apparent suspension in the middle or central region of the sky.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eye or pupil to roll.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes the black of the eye revolving as though in a spindle’s whirl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For wine to intoxicate someone so that he turns about.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative causative use describing disordered or revolving movement under intoxication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wind turbans around the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes repeated circular winding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put enough grease into broth for it to swim or circulate on the surface.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the grease’s circular movement on the broth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To roll or mumble the tongue, or to make a sound roll or rumble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to rolling the tongue in the mouth and, by extension, to a camel’s rolling or rumbling bray.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To moisten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially of moistening saliva; this is a reported Classical usage distinct from the sense of preserving or keeping something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mix, steep, or dissolve saffron in water while stirring it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes circular stirring during moistening or dissolution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To still or allay the boiling of a cooking-pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This may be done by sprinkling cold water on the contents or otherwise cooling them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persistently adhere to or continue an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى or with the affair as object for sustained engagement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something continue, last, endure, or remain; to maintain it continually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV use corresponding to the intransitive duration sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use associated with settled water in the bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To test or produce the sonorous quality of an arrow by turning or tapping it on the thumb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical expression concerning the sound of an arrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To await, expect, look for, or watch for something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively with an object; without an expressed object it may mean to pause or wait in expectation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act with moderation, gentleness, deliberation, or leisure; to seek or ask for continuance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of handling an affair deliberately or of requesting that a favor, condition, or state be prolonged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stoop the head with blood dropping from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare usage explained as formed by transposition from اِسْتَدْمَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continuous or repeatedly falling rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مَا زَالَتِ السَّمَاءُ دَوْمًا دَوْمًا for sustained rain of the type called دِيمَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The doum palm or a large tree bearing fan-shaped leaves and clusters like those of the date-palm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also extended by some speakers to certain lote trees or large trees generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single fruit of the doum palm, and by extension the corresponding unit noun for the tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is the singular unit form associated with دَوْمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A testicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative anatomical use based on comparison with the doum fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lasting, continuous, generally still rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classically described as rain continuing for a substantial period, often without thunder or lightning; reported minimum and maximum durations vary among authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Steady, continuous, and moderate activity or recurrence by comparison with lasting rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively for uninterrupted but not excessive work, and for trials or events arriving continuously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sea or a great river.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained as referring to water that continues and does not run out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vertigo or giddiness of the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions meaning that vertigo attacked or affected someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spinning top or a whirlpool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the toy that spins on the ground and to the sea’s central whirl where waves circle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Still or motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of water; this is a Classical sense distinct from the Quranic adjective meaning enduring or constant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going round, revolving, or circling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use applied to something in motion, alongside the contrary use for something still.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most continuous, lasting, or enduring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective derived from the duration sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continuous or lasting rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal designation for rain that continues.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained by the wine’s being kept until settled after fermentation, its abundance, age, or the prolonged drinking of it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stick or other implement used to still the boiling of a cooking-pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tool noun derived from the act of calming the pot’s boiling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land upon which continuous or soaking rains have fallen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of ground affected by rains of the type called دِيَم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having blood continually flowing from the nose, or suffering a continual nosebleed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources also give the broader gloss “bleeding from the nose.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waiting or watching; also, of birds, circling over something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle is used of birds circling overhead and, in another interpretation, of waiting or keeping watch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exceeding the usual bounds in an affair; striving or taking extraordinary pains in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare attributed usage associated with exerting unusual effort.

cautions: The Classical evidence preserves distinct, sometimes contrasting branches: duration and persistence, stillness, and circling or apparent suspension. The Quranic forms are restricted to the attested duration and constancy senses.
